items.title: 68426_Nellie Lutcher oral history interview
items.q: We call her Dina, it's a nickname for the family. She has a little group... She has six children... She writes a little, yes

ctx.x: I went back and listened to the previous reels, and a few things came up I wanted to ask you more about. At one point you mentioned that one of your sisters writes and has a group, and you didn't mention what sister.

Eugenia. We call her Dina, it's a nickname for the family. She has a little group, and it started with her children, some of her children. She has six children, incidentally. Three girls and three boys. One of the boys is a marvelous percussionist, and the other -- one of the other sons is inspired to be an actor. But anyway, when they were young children, in church -- she belongs to the Lutheran Church, they started as a group with the Negro History Week Program. She was the Chairman of this program. So she did…

was Black History Week, and what happened, and blah, blah, blah. And she did a marvelous job of it. And so it was so successful that she kept the little group together and they went to different churches, the Lutheran churches, and performed this little program. And then finally she sort of moved on into other areas, you know, and she's been -- they've been together now, this has been I guess, say, oh, about 8 or 10 years ago. And she's kept the little group together and they dance and perform, and of course the…
